root_cause.text: The `nf_conntrack_helper_unregister()` function passes NULL instead of the helper pointer to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy()`, causing the `expect_iter_me()` callback to fail to match and destroy expectations referencing the helper, leading to use-after-free when the helper object is freed while expectations still hold references to it.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 418 from `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, NULL);` to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, me);`. The CVE description explicitly states that "it passes NULL instead of the helper pointer as the data argument, so expect_iter_me() never matches any expectation and all of them survive the cleanup." Subsequently, "nfnl_cthelper_del() frees the helper object immediately" while expectations still reference it, causing the KASAN slab-use-after-free error when those expectations are later accessed.

candidates.rationale: This line passes NULL as the second argument to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy() instead of passing the helper pointer (me). The expect_iter_me() callback uses this argument to match and identify expectations associated with the specific helper being unregistered. By passing NULL, the callback cannot properly identify which expectations reference the helper, causing them to not be destroyed. This leads to use-after-free when the helper object is freed while expectations still hold references to it.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is clearly present in this commit. The `nf_conntrack_helper_unregister()` function calls `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, NULL)` on line 466, passing NULL as the second argument instead of passing the helper pointer `me`. The `expect_iter_me()` callback function (lines 440-454) expects to receive the helper pointer via the `data` parameter (line 442: `const struct nf_conntrack_helper *me = data;`), which it uses to match expectations that reference the helper. By passing NULL instead of `me`, the callback will receive NULL and fail to properly match and destroy expectations, leading to the use-after-free vulnerability described. The original code (lines 456-469 in the old version) correctly passed the helper pointer and checked both `exp->helper == me` and the help->helper comparison. The refactored code loses this critical parameter passing.
